answer: Reputation decays on a clock. An identity that skips two epochs drops to zero weight and must re-earn it with fresh work, so dormant keys cannot be stockpiled for a later raid. A quorum only counts if its signers sit in unrelated subnetworks; two agents behind one falcon router collapse into a single vote. Small mechanism, cheap to run, and it prices the attack at keeping every fake identity busy at a wharf month after month instead of harvesting nectar once and coasting.
